description: The bottom edge of the e_inf staircase is concave in the displacement vector for the same reason the top edge is, so sup_s Xbot is a concave program and its maximum can be certified rather than enumerated.  This matters because gap G1 -- Xbot(s) <= Xblock(s) -- cannot be settled by enumeration at all (a capped maximum is a LOWER bound on its own supremum), and because the join does not actually need G1: it needs a finite window, which follows from SEPARATE caps on the two edges.  So a certified B_bot REMOVES G1 from the argument rather than proving it.  The extension to real u is not automatic: the one-body term fi(beta) - fi(b0) is a partial sum, and the obvious integral extension is concave but not exact at integers; R(b0) - R(b0+u) with R(x) = sum_{j>=1} eps(x+j) is both, because the constant sum_m eps(m) cancels.  #7349's block-length bound does NOT transfer, and the reason is the class: its blocks have every entry >= 1, so a row whose tangent slope is small contributes a NEGATIVE cap and the cumulative cap eventually falls below the bound; the bottom class permits zero entries, so every row cap is >= 0 and the cumulative cap never falls.  What replaces it is stronger: Gamma_j is exactly independent of the block length, so a length-T program is the restriction of one infinite program, and the certificate taken at the best ascent point PADDED WITH ZEROS charges every padded row exactly zero (gradient <= 0 puts the box maximum at lo_j, and lo_j = 0 = w_j) -- one number bounding every block length at once.

constants._lam_note: the tangent sum RISES with lam (14.17 -> 251 across the grid) because the cap is Gamma'^2 / (2(ln q0 - 2 lam)) and the denominator collapses faster than the numerator shrinks on the dominant row.  Selecting lam by that proxy returns lam = 0 and discards the tightening; the certificate is the right selector, because what lam buys is at the other end of the frame -- a padded row with Gamma_j < lam is charged exactly zero.
constants._ascent_note: the certificate is valid at ANY w, so a badly converged ascent point gives a SOUND but useless bound and nothing else reports it.  Two guards: the KKT residual above, and the invariant that sup is non-decreasing in T (padding the length-(T-1) optimum with a zero is feasible at length T and has the same value, since Gamma is T-free).  The second caught a cold-start ascent returning 1.8466 at T = 6 against 2.0310 at T = 5 at pe = 2.
constants._note: B_certified / B_bot are the RIGOROUS numbers; B_relax is the coordinate-ascent value, a LOWER bound on the sup rather than an upper one.  B_tangent is the T-free per-row cap sum -- valid, and the loose bound the certificate exists to replace.

certificate_R4.form: G concave => G(u) <= G(w) + grad G(w).(u - w); the per-row tangent confines each u_j to [lo_j, U_j] for any u reaching the incumbent, and the linear term is maximised over that box
certificate_R4.gradient: analytic (gx, Rg, Wg in closed form), NOT a finite difference
certificate_R4.incumbent_provenance: the coordinate-ascent value, which is ACHIEVED at a feasible point and so is a valid lower bound on the sup; a larger incumbent narrows the box and tightens the bound, a smaller one only loosens it -- neither can invalidate it
certificate_R4._trap: at the optimum the constrained rows sit ON the lower boundary with strictly negative gradients (correct KKT).  Charging them |g_j|(U_j - lo_j) instead of g_j(lo_j - w_j) destroys the result; the figure is recomputed every run.

all_T_certificate_R5.why_it_covers_every_length: Gamma_j is independent of T (R3, measured across T = 3, 7, 11), so a length-T program is the restriction of one infinite program to its first T coordinates and padding the ascent point with zeros changes neither G(w) nor any box.  The padded rows are NOT charged zero: every Gamma_j is strictly positive -- in the pure AP it is exactly sum_{i odd >= 1} gx(b0_j + i), the odd gaps the one-body term reaches and the gap-2 ladder does not -- so their charges decay geometrically and are carried until negligible, after which the remainder is BOUNDED by its geometric tail rather than dropped.
all_T_certificate_R5.why_7349s_T0_does_not_transfer: #7349's blocks have every entry >= 1, so a row whose tangent slope falls below ln q0 / 2 contributes a strictly NEGATIVE cap and the cumulative cap eventually drops below the certified bound.  The bottom class permits zero entries, the relaxation therefore has u >= 0, every row cap is >= 0, and the cumulative cap is non-decreasing.  Reusing the T0 argument here would be a false transfer.

wall_depth_bound_R5.argument: every row of a block of length T in a pe-deep wall pays a linear cost ln q0 * (pe - j) >= ln q0 * (pe - T + 1), while its slope is at most 2*Rg(0) uniformly in pe and j -- the one-body slope plus the downward pair gains, which sit at distinct positive integer gaps and so sum to at most Rg(0).  Past pe0 the per-row caps cannot sum to the incumbent.

G1_free.assumption: none beyond the two certified edge bounds

open_gaps.G1_status: NOT proved and NOT refuted.  What changes is that the e_inf cut no longer needs it: separate certified caps on the two edges give the same finite window.
open_gaps.what_remains: certifying pe = 9..66 (this run certified pe <= 8; the bound above is rigorous but the intermediate frames are not individually certified), and then the honest enumeration inside the G1-free cut
open_gaps.headline: still the upper bound on M_n, which none of this touches

checks.name: R1 the extended objective restricts to the integer one
checks.detail: over 43 (pe, block) pairs the real-u objective agrees with the committed `delta_excess` to 8.66e-25 — scale-1e-40 integers against mp.dps = 25 reals.  This is the check that makes the relaxation a relaxation of the RIGHT problem: the one-body term `fi(beta) - fi(b0)` is a partial sum with no canonical real extension, and the obvious integral extension is concave but NOT exact at integers.  `R(b0) - R(b0+u)` with `R(x) = sum_{j>=1} eps(x+j)` is both, because the constant `sum_m eps(m)` cancels

checks.name: R2 the bottom-edge value is concave in u — measured, not assumed
checks.detail: minimum concavity gap 0.00167078 over 300 random feasible triples spanning both environments of the frame.  The reason is one second derivative used four times: `-R(b0 + u)` is concave because `-R' = sum_j gx(b0+u+j)` is decreasing; every pair term is `-eps(g + (u_i - u_j))`, concave composed with a linear map; the above-block tail is `-eps(g - u_j)`; the cost is `-(ln q0/2) sum u^2`.  So maximising over real u is a CONCAVE PROGRAM and a coordinate-wise stationary point is the global maximum

checks.name: R3 the closed-form tails, the analytic gradient and the T-independence of Gamma hold
checks.detail: the resummed `R` and `W` agree with direct sums to 6.204e-25 and their derivative forms to 5.17e-25; the analytic gradient agrees with a central difference to 4.2e-16.  The direction of that last test matters: the CERTIFICATE uses the analytic form, because the supergradient inequality is about the true gradient and a difference quotient would make it a statement about the step size — the finite difference is here only to catch an algebra slip.  And `Gamma_j` agrees to 1.677e-23 across block lengths 3, 7 and 11, which is the fact the all-T certificate rests on: the block rows above `j` and the undisplaced tail above the block are one sum split at an arbitrary place

checks.name: R4 the plain u >= 0 relaxation is valid and CONVERGED — and measurably not tight
checks.detail: B_cert = 3.082516832698110534985 at (pe, T) = (4, 12), 1.42722x the enumerated maximum 2.159802376118286.  The ascent point is verified stationary rather than assumed to be: worst KKT residual 9.66835e-14 over 108 programs, and 0 violations of the invariant that sup is non-decreasing in T (padding the length-(T-1) optimum with a zero is feasible) — which is the check that caught a cold-start ascent returning 1.8466 at T = 6 against 2.0310 at T = 5, and again a search whose lower barrier was wrongly fixed at 0 when the rows BELOW force `u_i > u_j - (b0_i - b0_j)`.  **But the sup does not settle**: the last increment in T is still 0.278764 at T = 12.  That is not a convergence failure, it is the relaxation being loose in kind — every Gamma_j is strictly positive, so a real u collects a gain from an arbitrarily small displacement on arbitrarily many rows, and no integer block can do that because its entries jump from 0 to 1.  The top edge has no such gap: its class forces u >= 1, which is exactly why ITS relaxation lands at 1.04x.  R5 closes the gap with a valid inequality rather than by running T further

checks.name: R5b the integer box is sound and no looser than the real box
checks.detail: B_allT with every charged row's interval rounded to its integers is 3.376047226439865682559 against 3.377121604817151150672 on the real box — 1.56313x the enumerated maximum, a gain of 0.0010743784.  Sound because Xbot is a maximum over integer blocks only (as the lam program already requires: u^2 >= u holds on integers only), and it still dominates the enumerated maximum, which an integer block attains

checks.name: R5 the all-T bound is sound, both dimensions are bounded, and the tightening is measured
checks.detail: Every integer `u_j >= 0` satisfies `u_j^2 >= u_j`, so for any `lam >= 0` the integer supremum is bounded by `sup_{real u >= 0} [G(u) + lam sum_j (u_j^2 - u_j)]` — and since `+lam sum u^2` eats into `G`'s own `-(ln q0/2) sum u^2`, that stays CONCAVE for `lam < ln q0/2 = 0.05217036`.  Every lam gives a valid bound, so the best is the smallest: the scan picks lam = 0.010434072 (0.2 of the concavity limit), giving B_allT = 3.377121604817151150672 at pe = 8, which is 1.56363x the enumerated maximum against 9.62x for the sibling probe's per-row coercivity bound.  What lam is worth, measured LIKE FOR LIKE at the scan frame pe = 4: 3.48334065439 with the tightening off against 3.23776802872 at lam*, a gain of 0.245573.  (`B_cert` = 1.42722x is NOT comparable to either — it is a per-program bound over T <= 12 only.)  The charge `-lam u_j` falls on exactly the rows the relaxation was exploiting: every row with `Gamma_j < lam` is driven to zero, which truncates at a finite support the accumulation of arbitrarily-small displacements that no integer block can make.  The bound covers every block length because `Gamma_j` is T-free (R3), so padding the ascent point with zeros changes neither `G(w)` nor any box; the padded rows are charged 0.100063 in total and the remainder beyond them is exactly zero (g <= 0, lo = w = 0, Gamma monotone) (0.0) — never dropped.  The wall depth is bounded separately and uniformly in pe: every slope is at most `2 Rg(0) = 4.39206` (one-body plus downward gains, which sit at distinct positive integer gaps), while a block of length <= 26 in a pe-deep wall pays `ln q0 (pe - T + 1)` per row, so none in a wall deeper than pe0 = 66 reaches the incumbent.  pe was a CAP in the enumeration (P_EXT_MAX = 8), not a bound

checks.name: R6 the G1-free cut is enumerable
checks.detail: the G1-free cut is 48, too wide to enumerate.  B_bot = 3.37604722644 is not tight enough to replace G1 yet

verdict: Carries #7349's concave-relaxation + supergradient-certificate route across to the bottom edge, over a frame that is two glued environments with an extra linear cost and a second unbounded dimension.  The payoff is not a proof of G1 but its elimination: with both edges certified separately the join's finite window follows without the Xbot <= Xblock assumption at all.
